sense: a made-up answer from an AI

evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.5: opīniōnum commenta dēlet diēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Classically an invention, a fiction, a falsehood (see fiction), from comminīscor, to make up something untrue; used of an AI’s made-up answer it is modern, and ours. English “hallucination” is a metaphor Latin need not copy: what the machine does is make things up, and Latin says so.

terms.gloss: to make up, to invent (something untrue)
evidence: Plaut. Asin. 102: fabricāre quidvīs, quidvīs comminīscere
Cic. N.D. 2.59: Epicūrus monogrammōs deōs et nihil agentēs commentus est (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The verb, for “it’s hallucinating”: māchina comminīscitur. Lewis & Short notes that it is said classically of what is untrue.

phrases.latin: Hoc nōn est vērum; māchina id commenta est.
phrases.english: That isn’t true; the AI made it up.

phrases.latin: Cavē; māchinae saepe commenta prō vērīs narrant.
phrases.english: Be careful; machines often tell made-up things as if they were true.
